keyFindings.description: The gone-pod report counts every blocking claim not in the round as lost: a claim an earlier sweep's end already reached (while another is held in Resume), or a role first started in the new pod, is named as having lost work although it answered or never ran in the dead pod. Reproduced (DeepReview8 held-Resume test; RSM8 new-role test); not a regression, but the delta's prose says the report no longer depends on order.

The new drop of a left round's ask returns before the askFirst reset; after a restart the next task is confirmed by an unrelated turn and retired unsent. Regression from de49ef1c; reproduced; fix verified in a copy.

A round whose pod no live claim records still waits for turns in the new pod before asking PodDrift; when the new pod has drifted and a turn runs, the round over the dead pod stays open, answered workers' tasks are held and a late notice can fire. Reproduced.
The left-pod refusal names PodRound(new pod) as 'the round of that pod', a round that does not exist; a worker answering it is refused again.
A suspension's letGo clears the locator, so a frozen claim's late answer from the new-pod process is accepted once suspended (narrow: needs a stop mid-turn).
Round 7 asked to keep R2, R2b and R3 as daemon-level tests on the machines' own relaunch; only supervise-level tests were added.
